slot.brief: Match defect types (Schottky, Frenkel, metal-excess, metal-deficiency) with examples and effects on density/conductivity at moderate level.

stem: Which description correctly identifies these point-defect effects in ionic solids?
options: Schottky pair in NaCl lowers density; Frenkel defect in AgCl leaves density unchanged; metal-excess ZnO is n-type; metal-deficient FeO is p-type
Schottky pair in NaCl leaves density unchanged; Frenkel defect in AgCl leaves density unchanged; metal-excess ZnO is n-type; metal-deficient FeO is p-type
Schottky pair in NaCl lowers density; Frenkel defect in AgCl lowers density; metal-excess ZnO is n-type; metal-deficient FeO is p-type
Schottky pair in NaCl lowers density; Frenkel defect in AgCl leaves density unchanged; metal-excess ZnO is p-type; metal-deficient FeO is n-type

verdicts.working: Schottky defects remove ions and lower density; Frenkel defects preserve mass and density. Metal-excess ZnO is n-type, while metal-deficient FeO is p-type.

working:
Schottky defects remove ions from lattice sites and lower density; Frenkel defects displace ions within the crystal, leaving density unchanged. Oxygen-deficient ZnO has electrons (n-type); cation-deficient FeO has holes (p-type).

Independent check: Schottky defects remove ions and lower density; Frenkel defects preserve mass and density. Metal-excess ZnO is n-type, while metal-deficient FeO is p-type.
solution:
Schottky defects remove ions from lattice sites, lowering density; Frenkel defects displace ions within the crystal, leaving density unchanged. Metal-excess ZnO is $n$-type, while metal-deficient FeO is $p$-type.
Thus, all four descriptions in (A) are correct.
